newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Parliament approves Kuwait Airways budget.
newsitem.headline: Parliament approves Kuwait Airways budget.

text.p: Parliament on Tuesday approved the 1997/98 budget for Kuwait Airways Corp (KAC) which was earlier rejected after MPs alleged corruption and mismangement resulting in huge losses.

After rejecting it on Monday, parliament passed the budget for the national flag carrier for the fiscal year starting July 1, 1997 with a projected deficit of 10.55 million dinars ($34.65 million) compared with a forecast deficit for the previous year of 29.21 million dinars.
KAC, which is being considered for privatisation, in March put total income at 98.5 million dinars in the six months to December 1996 compared with expenditures of 111 million dinars.

Some 9.1 million dinars of the deficit were spent on debt servicing. KAC, which lost 86 percent of its assets during the 1990-91 Iraqi occupation of Kuwait, spends about 20 million dinars a year on financing debts of about 230 million dinars.
KAC made a loss of 35 million dinars in the fiscal year ending June 30, 1996 compared with 27.9 million dinars the previous year.
Parlaiment approved the 1997/98 budget after cutting total expenditure by 6.04 million dinars and raising revenue projections by three million dinars.
Total income was amended to 209.35 million dinars and expenditure was cut to 219.90 million dinars.

Cost of aircraft operations was projected at 93.32 million dinars. KAC has a fleet of 15 Airbus Industries aircraft, all bought after the 1991 Gulf War, and two Boeing Co BA.CN 747s which will be replaced by two Boeing 777s on order.

KAC Chairman Ahmad al-Meshari earlier told Reuters the airline could return to profit if the government allowed it to match regional air fare rates and helped finance post-Gulf War reconstruction costs.

It presented the government with a three-stage plan over 18 months to raise fares between 15 percent and 25 percent -- a move which Meshari said, if approved, would bring in 17 million dinars a year in added revenue.
KAC's assets were estimated at 723 million dinars at the end of 1996 -- a rise of 179 percent since 1991 when a U.S.-led military coalition forced Iraq out of Kuwait.
